gaps.fact: The fourteen Second Growths of 1855 with their communes. The article names eleven of them across its commune notes (Cos d'Estournel, Montrose, the three Léovilles, Ducru-Beaucaillou, Gruaud Larose, the two Pichons, Rauzan-Ségla, Brane-Cantenac) and never Lascombes, Durfort-Vivens or Rauzan-Gassies; no question of either bank asks a Second Growth's commune.
Cru Bourgeois was created in 1932 (the Court's 1930s). The Régionale chapter and the article give the three tiers and the five year cycle but never the founding date, and no question asks it.
Pomerol's top producers as the Court lists them: Lafleur and Clos l'Église appear once each in an article place note and are asked nowhere; the banks drill Pétrus and Le Pin only.

The top Bordeaux vintages of the last fifteen years and why they are top. The Codex holds no vintage list by house rule (nothing volatile), so a candidate has nothing to drill for this cell or for the Business row's price differences by vintage.

Black rot as the second harmful rot (the Court pairs it with grey rot against noble rot) and spring frost as a Bordeaux hazard: the Village bank asks grey rot (c-s5ui9nfp) and the article mentions spring frost in a clause, but no question asks either for Bordeaux.
Bordeaux as a slave trade port, and Bordeaux as the largest region of AOP wine production in France today: neither sentence of the Court's History cell appears in a chapter, an article or a question.
The Court reads the climate as maritime at the coast shading to continental inland; the Codex says maritime only and never places the Right Bank or Entre-Deux-Mers on that gradient.

Why the classic pairings work: the Régionale bank has lamb with red Bordeaux and the Village bank Sauternes with foie gras, but no question reasons from tannin, acidity or sweetness to a Bordeaux style, and no Pessac-Léognan white or Pomerol pairing is asked.

errors.where: js/data-primers.js, PRIMERS cat Bordeaux, fact Entre-Deux-Mers: "the appellation covers dry white only, mostly Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon; the reds of the same land sell as Bordeaux or Bordeaux Supérieur"
errors.claim: Entre-Deux-Mers AOP is a dry white appellation and its reds can only be Bordeaux or Bordeaux Supérieur.
errors.correction: Since the 2023 vintage Entre-deux-Mers also covers red wine under its own stricter rules (a minimum of 4,500 vines per hectare, Merlot, the two Cabernets, Malbec and Petit Verdot, eighteen months before release, first bottles from January 2025); reds that do not meet them still sell as Bordeaux or Bordeaux Supérieur. The region article (law, tiers; places; traps) and the Régionale stem i-yputip89 already teach dry white and red, so the Village chapter contradicts its own article.
errors.source: INAO, cahier des charges AOC Entre-deux-Mers as modified in 2023 (the red approved by the INAO committee in 2023); reports at janeanson.com and wine-business-international.com; the Entre-deux-Mers growers' page cited by the article itself.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 63 (Bordeaux), Village 54 (Bordeaux), 117 in all. Beyond the map, nine Sauternes stems sit under Dessert & Sweet Wines, three under Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet and four Bergerac and Sauternes stems under Sweet Wines; nine Bordeaux estates are asked under Producers & Icons and five Bordeaux episodes under History & Figures. The Certified column is strongly served on classification, appellation geography, soil and the trade; weakest on the Second Growths, the Pomerol producers beyond Pétrus and Le Pin, vintages and the two History sentences. Two readings to carry when our own copy is written: the Village stem c-y2kbp0cy keys that the 1855 red list has been altered twice (Cantemerle added in 1856, Mouton raised in 1973), which is historically sound, while the Court teaches only one change (Mouton 1973) and an exam key will follow the Court; and the Court prints the Saint-Émilion classification as 1959 where the Codex (chapter fact 3, article law) says 1955, the year the first list was published, so a candidate should answer the Court's year on the paper and know ours. One search spent, on the Entre-deux-Mers red; the Cru Bourgeois 2025 renewal is taken from the article's own dated source. Nothing else in the Court's Bordeaux law cells has moved since 8.2023.
